purpose: Quantify VIIRS clear-land observation coverage across route buffers and diagnose frozen JMA alerts on selected report dates.

protocol.cohort: All eight routes on 27 dates where the national SNMF report explicitly listed no fires in 2024.
protocol.spatial_unit: Grid samples within 10 km of each complete route polyline.
protocol.clear_land_fraction: FireMask class 5 with QA land divided by all route-buffer grid samples.
protocol.sensor_choice: Use the single available sensor with the highest clear-land fraction for each route-day; do not union sensor pixels because source audits retain aggregate counts only.
protocol.fire_detection: Any FireMask class 7-9 from any available same-day sensor.
protocol.model_alignment: Frozen JMA score at diagnostic threshold 0.1; no threshold tuning in this analysis.
protocol.independence_unit: Report dates are clustered when consecutive; route-days within a date and sensor passes are dependent.

limitations: SNMF reported start date does not specify exact active-fire time during each VIIRS observation.
A clear-land no-detection at the pass does not negate an official fire event; timing, containment, fire size and sensor sensitivity can explain disagreement.
This selected event cohort measures coincidence and observation quality, not a definitive sensitivity or false-negative rate.

interpretation: High clear-land fraction supports a well-observed VIIRS non-detection for the sensor-detection target, not proof of physical fire absence. This selected negative-report cohort has no detected fire positives, is clustered in time, and cannot estimate fire-alert precision, recall, or prevalence. JMA alerts without VIIRS detections are disagreement cases, not confirmed false alarms.
